artworks.title: Cave of Trophonius
artworks.description: Smirke's Yale drawing: the oracular cave at Lebadeia — Trophonius' chasm as Romantic ruin, the place Pausanias said no consulter ever smiled again.

artworks.title: The Hercyna and the Cave of Trophonius
artworks.description: Belle's landscape of the Hercyna and Trophonius' lair — nineteenth-century travel art for Boeotia's most dreaded oracle.

artworks.title: Oracular Cavern of Trophonius
artworks.description: Skene's view of the oracular cavern — the Lebadean descent that turned a builder-hero into a chthonic voice.

artworks.title: Trophonius
artworks.description: Nineteenth-century illustration of Trophonius — the architect who became an oracle, remembered as a face in print culture.

popCulture.title: Description of Greece
popCulture.creator: Pausanias
popCulture.description: Pausanias' full rite of consultation at Lebadeia — honey-cakes, the descent, and the rule that no one laughs afterward.

popCulture.title: Trophonius
popCulture.description: Builder of Apollo's treasury who sank into the earth and rose as Boeotia's oracle — the cave that answers underground.
